turn_text: You mentioned this is a bipartisan effort. Well, let me tell you, I serve on the appropriations committee, the subcommittee, the funds on health care, labor, health, human services. And I'm very sad to say we see budget cuts in those accounts that really are the accounts in the health care service care prevention and treatment and research accounts that we need to accomplish our goals of ending HIV and AIDS by 2030. And we're close. And we're close, but I see these cuts coming forward, which are going to set us back. And so what we're trying to do now is restore these cuts. In addition, over 40% of those who need medical care get their care through Medicaid. But yet this administration is trying to cut Medicaid and will not expand Medicaid in many of the states where people need access to health care through Medicaid. And so on one hand, you have really this administration, Robin Peter, to pay for their cutting, PEPFAR, their cutting, the global fund. And so I see these cuts as being a real signal that you know, while they're trying to say one thing, yet they're doing another. Now, having said that, we're working with CDC and with other entities within the government, our civil servants, people who've been there a while and been there since the beginning of this epidemic to try to craft this plan in a way that's targeted to the states and the counties that have the highest rates of infections and target the resources, but also make sure that the money, any money goes to organizations on the ground that really know how to do this work. And so I'm asking CDC and others to come to my community and through communities around the country to have listening sessions so that they can hear from people directly. with regard to what needs to be in this new quote plan that the Trump administration is putting out.
